chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from 'Amr ibn 'Uthman, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him)

(He narrated) similar to it, and added to it: 'So he does not stop calling out until he is placed in his grave. So when he enters his pit, the soul returns to his body and the two Angels of the Grave come to him, so they test him.' He (the narrator) said, 'And Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) would weep when he mentioned this Hadith.'

key_terms.مَلَكَا الْقَبْرِ: The two Angels of the Grave (Munkar and Nakir)

ai.seo_question: What happens to the soul and the deceased in the grave according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) details the immediate return of the soul to the body upon burial, preceding the interrogation by Munkar and Nakir, a moment so profound it moved the Imam to tears. It underscores the Shia emphasis on the intermediate state (Barzakh) as a time of active accountability where the soul re-enters the physical form for judgment. This event serves as a spiritual wakefulness for the living, reminding them that death is not an end but a transition to a new phase of existence.
